extraction.name: WikiText
extraction.description: A new benchmark dataset for language modeling constructed using text extracted from Wikipedia, provided in two sizes: WikiText-2 and WikiText-103.
extraction.url: Available for download at the WikiText dataset site
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher
extraction.citeAs: Merity, Stephen; Xiong, Caiming; Bradbury, James; Socher, Richard. Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models. arXiv:1609.07843v1, 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed using text extracted from Wikipedia. The authors selected articles only fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia. This resulted in 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles. The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consisted of Wikipedia articles, specifically articles meeting the Good or Featured article criteria, extracted from Wikipedia markup via the Wikipedia API.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Specific sections which primarily featured lists were removed by default. Other minor bugs, such as sort keys and Edit buttons that leaked in from the HTML, were also removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with formula tokens. A vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3, and words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the unknown token.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Extracting the raw text from Wikipedia mark-up was performed despite extensive macros. After extraction, list-heavy sections were removed by default, sort keys and Edit buttons leaking from HTML were removed, and mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with formula tokens. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer, slightly augmented to further split numbers (8,600 to 8 @,@ 600) and with some additional minor fixes. Following Chelba et al. (2013), a vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3. Words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the unknown token. The dataset was provided in the same format and following the same conventions as the PTB dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Articles were selected only if they fit the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia. These articles have been reviewed by humans and are considered well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral in point of view, and stable.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors hope this new dataset can serve as a platform to improve handling of rare words and the usage of long term dependencies in language modeling.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper discusses limitations of the Penn Treebank dataset rather than WikiText: PTB is all lower case, stripped of punctuation, and limited to a vocabulary of only 10k words, making it unrealistic for real language use and problematic for accurately predicting rare words such as named entities. No explicit limitations of WikiText itself are stated.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is introduced as a benchmark for language modeling, to evaluate how well language models can exploit longer contexts and deal with more realistic vocabularies and larger corpora. It is used for training, validation, and testing, with WikiText-2 and WikiText-103 provided as benchmark options.
